cards.title: After Automation: what work becomes when agents do the tasks
cards.whyNow: An essay-length frame for the question under all of Field Theory Labs: when agents absorb execution, what does the human's day consist of — taste, direction, judgment loops. Reading it may sharpen what the Goals feed's human feedback is actually for.
cards.goal: Read After Automation and extract its claims into the Field Theory library as a brief that answers one pointed question: which human judgments does the essay say survive automation, and does the Goals feed capture exactly those (usefulness, timing, taste) or proxies of them. If the essay names judgment types the feedback schema misses, propose the smallest schema addition to goal_feedback that would capture one of them. Success criterion: the brief exists in the library with a direct keep-or-change recommendation for the feedback schema, citing at least 3 specific passages.
cards.firstTest: Fetch the essay and read it with the goal_feedback schema open beside it.
cards.scoreNote: matched "idea generation agent"; strongest axes evidence + leverage; category unclassified

cards.title: Mercury Command: agentic OS grafted onto trusted product UX
cards.whyNow: Mercury shipped agent capability inside the surfaces its users already trust, rather than as a separate chat app. That is the same integration thesis as Field Theory's: agents reached through Library, Voice, and feeds rather than a chatbox.
cards.goal: Study how Command surfaces agentic actions inside Mercury's existing UX (entry points, confirmation patterns, how it shows work-in-progress and results), then audit Field Theory's surfaces for the one place an agent action is most naturally reachable but currently isn't — the Goals feed's Pursue button being the live candidate, since it currently copies a goal to the pasteboard rather than dispatching it. Scope the smallest dispatch path from Pursue to an actual agent run. Success is empirical: one pursued goal travels from phone tap to a started agent run without manual pasting, demonstrated end to end at least once with tap-to-run latency under 60 seconds recorded.
cards.firstTest: Write down the current Pursue-to-execution path (tap → pasteboard → manual /goal paste) and mark each manual step.

cards.title: Intelligence is getting cheaper — the cost curves
cards.whyNow: a16z's charts quantify the collapse in per-token intelligence cost. For Labs, the actionable question is which Field Theory pipelines were designed under cost assumptions that are now false.
cards.goal: Re-audit Field Theory's model-usage economics against current prices: pull the actual model calls made by the recurring pipelines (Theories scans, ft possible runs, enrichment passes), compute what each costs per run today, and identify which quality-reducing compromises (smaller models, skipped stages, truncated context) were made for cost reasons that no longer hold. Upgrade the one compromise with the best quality-per-dollar case and measure the difference on real output. Success criterion: a cost table for at least three pipelines exists with real per-run numbers, and one upgraded pipeline shows a blind-judged quality improvement at a computed acceptable cost delta.
cards.firstTest: Instrument or tally one Theories scan's actual token usage and price it at current rates.
cards.scoreNote: matched "idea generation agent"; strongest axes evidence + leverage; category unclassified
